why: The budget part says finishing long problems before the cap is a policy RL learned by training truncated rollouts as negatives, so RL solves 16 of the 27 T1 cap hits (result-5e17a6); Think-SFT has no reward and hits the cap 25 times, mostly on RL's longest quartile, so it should rescue a few fewer, partly offset by its strength on long problems (+6 vs RL in Q4).

Under the mechanism, base cap hits are long unsolved problems that only a policy of finishing before the cap rescues; a reward-free imitator that caps on the same long problems should solve them less often than difficulty-matched finished-wrong problems, giving a modest negative excess with wide noise from only about 27 cap-hit problems.
